domains.name: Frontier Doctrine
domains.description: Settlers move out at breakneck pace, and the realm can coordinate one extra expansion at a time.

domains.name: Dwarf Kingdom
domains.description: Forts pop up overnight and cost a pittance to keep.

domains.name: Dewildernisation
domains.description: A concerted imperial campaign to push back the wilds. Raiders strike harder against barbarian holdings, dealing significantly more damage in frontier combat.

domains.name: Mercantile Charter
domains.description: Your first three cities become the commercial heart of the realm.

domains.name: Clockwork Stipend
domains.description: Imperial machinery allocates dedicated logistics slots for one chosen resource (titanium, umbrite, or crystal), regardless of the map.

domains.name: Cogwork Foundries
domains.description: Steam-driven assembly lines and clockwork cranes turn every blueprint into a running production line. Town support buildings build 25% faster.

domains.name: Garrison Doctrine
domains.description: Every fort you control is dug in, reinforced, and permanently manned. Forts you control fight with 50% extra defense.

domains.name: Steam Vanguard
domains.description: Boiler-fed assault columns commit before the enemy can dig in. Attacks resolve 5s faster, and one more muster flag can be held at once.

domains.name: Scholastic Exchanges
domains.description: Trade routes carry knowledge as well as goods.

domains.name: Crystal Network
domains.description: Observatories project safe control deep into exposed territory.

domains.name: Provincial Governors
domains.description: Governors uncap the treasury: town and dock gold reserves both grow 25% larger.

domains.name: War Foundries
domains.description: Armories mass-produce siege gear: attacks against forts hit harder, and your muster lines hold two more flags.

domains.name: Supply State
domains.description: A wide empire keeps moving because its logistics do.

domains.name: Merchant Houses
domains.description: Every dock you link into the trade network pays more the bigger the network gets, and your first three cities keep more of the profit.

domains.name: Provincial Nurseries
domains.description: The first three cities grow harder and taller than the rest of the realm — and two of them are fed for free.

domains.name: Imperial Roads
domains.description: Administration and movement fuse into one expansion machine, and every connected town pays its neighbors better.

domains.name: Signal Bastions
domains.description: Every fort becomes a garrisoned watchtower: forts and towns alike see much further across the frontier.

domains.name: Siege State
domains.description: Outposts become breaching engines: attacks against forts hit far harder, and muster lines hold two more flags.

domains.name: Treasury State
domains.description: Your first three settled towns and their support buildings require no food, and the treasury holds more gold.

domains.name: Hidden Hand
domains.description: State intelligence cuts every observatory ability's cooldown in half.

domains.name: Imperial Expansion
domains.description: A sprawling empire expands on every front at once and still holds a dangerous frontier with an extra flag to spare.

domains.name: Titanium Dominion
domains.description: Military force becomes your primary language: attack and defense are stronger everywhere, and your own forts hold the line even harder.

domains.name: Enduring Realm
domains.description: A compact empire survives through elite core cities and towns that never go hungry.

domains.name: Golden Hegemony
domains.description: A rich, tightly connected network of cities and ports bankrolls the empire.

domains.name: Oracle State
domains.description: Information superiority becomes empire superiority: observatories reach further, recharge faster, and towns see deep into the frontier.
